papers.title: RL unknotter, hard unknots and unknotting number
papers.abstract: We train a reinforcement learning agent to simplify hard unknot diagrams and pair it with a learned crossing selector to search for short unknotting sequences. Three examples found by the agent lead to an infinite family of prime two-bridge knots of unknotting number three whose connected sums with the figure-eight knot also have unknotting number three, and fifteen new unknotting upper bounds were found on the set of prime knots up to 13 crossings.

papers.title: Rigidity for Families of Abelian Varieties over $\mathcal{M}_{g,n}$
papers.abstract: We provide a new proof of Farb's theorem on the global rigidity of the period map $\mathcal{M}_{g,n} \to \mathcal{A}_g$. We extend this classification to essentially include the period map for $\mathcal{M}_{2,n}$. We also provide a classification of holomorphic maps $\mathcal{M}_g \to \mathcal{A}_{h}$ for $h \leq 2g-1$. The only nonconstant maps in this range are given by taking the Jacobian of a curve and attaching a fixed Abelian variety. In addition to the group theory of the mapping class group, we make extensive use of the theory of variations of Hodge structures and the birational geometry on $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_2$.

papers.title: Counterexamples to Grad's conjecture of any knot type
papers.abstract: We construct smooth magnetohydrostatic counterexamples to Grad's conjecture in toroidal domains of arbitrary knot type. The magnetic field is nonvanishing, and nested pressure tori fill the domain outside a nondegenerate magnetic axis. The equilibria have trivial Euclidean symmetry group and occur in smooth families of inequivalent configurations. On each regular pressure torus the magnetic flow is smoothly conjugate to a linear flow with any prescribed positive constant slope. A variation of this argument gives equilibria of arbitrary knot type with twist (that is, nonconstant rotational transform) and any finite regularity. A key ingredient of the proof is a deformation method that creates knot topology from axial symmetry by separating the sheets of a covering immersion into a braid, which may be useful in other deformation problems.

papers.title: Character variety of the punctured sphere and the determinantal variety
papers.abstract: We show that the SL(2;C) character variety of the n-punctured sphere is described via the determinantal variety defined by an n x n symmetric matrix of rank at most 4 whose entries are the traces of simple closed curves on the surface. This result generalizes the Fricke-Klein-Vogt relations to arbitrary n, and we determine the structure of the kernel of the associated matrix.

papers.title: Canonical metrics on punctured spheres, II: compactified moduli spaces of black holes
papers.abstract: Let $g_{\mathfrak{p}_{\ell}}$ denote the canonical scalar-flat metric on $S^n\setminus \mathfrak{p}_{\ell}$ introduced in Part~I, which for $n=3$ corresponds to the Brill--Lindquist initial data for $\ell$ black holes, and let $\eta\in H_{\ell}$ be its associated mass matrix. In this paper, we investigate the asymptotic behavior of the metrics and the mass matrix $\eta$ as subsets of punctures collide. Such collisions cause every mass to diverge; if a cluster $A$ of black holes collapses at a relative scale $t$, the mass matrix satisfies $\eta=E(A)\ln(1/t)+O(1)$, diverging along an explicit ray $E(A)\in H_{\ell}$. For nested families of clusters, this degeneracy structure naturally organizes into a space of rooted trees. Subtracting the divergence gives a renormalized mass matrix which extends smoothly to every stratum of the Axelrod--Singer compactified moduli space $\overline{M}{}^{\,\mathrm{AS}}_\ell= \overline C_{\ell-1}(\mathbb{R}^n)/\mathrm O(n)$ and splits naturally into one mass matrix per vertex of the bubble tree. Geometrically, at each vertex carrying punctures the suitably rescaled metrics converge to a complete scalar-flat metric with the nodes filled in, adjacent such pieces being joined by Schwarzschild necks, and the renormalized matrix acting as its mass data. For $n=3$, the necks contain minimal spheres, which are common apparent horizons of the merging holes. At vertices bearing two holes, we determine on which side of the limiting horizon each node lies, and we formulate as a conjecture the resulting criterion for a neck to be a component of the outermost horizon. We also compare the mass lower bound of Part~I with the Riemannian Penrose inequality. Because the mass matrix is invariant under rotations of the bubbles, it lives on a Deligne--Mumford-type quotient of the compactification.

papers.title: Delaunay Combinatorics of the Moduli and Teichm\"uller Space of Closed Genus-Two Riemann Surfaces
papers.abstract: Every closed Riemann surface of genus two is hyperelliptic, so it is determined by six branch points on the sphere, which become cone points of angle pi in the quotient orbifold metric. The Delaunay decomposition of these cone points, dual to the Voronoi diagram of the Weierstrass points, gives a trivalent graph with eight vertices, twelve edges and six faces. We classify these graphs. When the dual triangulation is simple there are exactly two types, dual to the octahedron and to a stacked triangulation, with orientation-preserving automorphism groups of orders 24 and 2, and we determine the Whitehead-move (diagonal-flip) orbit connecting them. Allowing bigons, the orbit closes at exactly twenty types. Iterated edge contraction from the two simple types gives a seven-level hierarchy of 2, 6, 22, 32, 22, 5 and 1 types, ending at two vertices joined by six parallel edges; closing under both contraction and expansion gives all 280 maps on the sphere with six vertices and no vertex of degree one. The rank of the linear cone-angle system of each type equals the real dimension 6 of the Teichm\"uller space. We realize both simple types by explicit hyperbolic cone spheres, in closed form for the octahedral type, build the corresponding genus-two surfaces by cutting and doubling, and show that the boundary x_e = 0 of the angle system is exactly the concyclicity of four branch points. The classification, the automorphism groups and the flip orbit are formally verified in Lean 4, and every enumeration is reproduced by an independent program, which also determines which types are realized by Delaunay decompositions.

papers.title: Equivariant intersection cohomology of some $4$-dimensional locally standard $T$-pseudomanifolds
papers.abstract: Locally standard $T$-pseudomanifolds are singular analogues of quasitoric manifolds. In this paper, we study a certain class of four-dimensional locally standard $T^2$-pseudomanifolds over convex polygons. We establish an Orlik-Raymond type classification and study their ordinary and equivariant cohomology, as well as their intersection and equivariant intersection cohomology. We also introduce ring structures on middle-perversity intersection cohomology and equivariant intersection cohomology via change of perversity. We show that these rings can be described in terms of the cohomology and equivariant cohomology of associated nonsingular spaces, which are quasitoric manifolds or $S^4$. Furthermore, we give combinatorial descriptions of the equivariant cohomology and equivariant intersection cohomology in terms of labelled graphs.

papers.title: Fundamental groups of closed four-manifolds with positive biorthogonal curvature
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove that a group is the fundamental group of a closed, connected, oriented smooth four-manifold admitting a metric of positive biorthogonal curvature if and only if it is finitely presented. This answers a question of Bettiol. The manifold can be chosen to be stably parallelizable, hence spin with vanishing signature, and with Euler characteristic $2(1-p+q)$, where $p$ and $q$ are the numbers of generators and of nontrivial relators in a given finite presentation. Moreover, we show that the class of closed oriented four-manifolds admitting positive biorthogonal curvature is closed under surgery along embedded circles. As applications, we obtain metrics of positive biorthogonal curvature on the boundary of every compact oriented five-manifold that has a handle decomposition with handles of index at most two, which includes every oriented $S^2$-bundle over a closed oriented surface. We also obtain such metrics on $Y\times S^1$ for every closed orientable three-manifold $Y$ of positive scalar curvature and, after connected sum with copies of $S^2\times S^2$, on a large class of four-manifolds with arbitrary fundamental group. Finally, we show that for the fundamental group of a finite aspherical two-dimensional complex $X$ the minimal Euler characteristic of such manifolds equals $2\chi(X)$.

papers.title: Local limit theorems and counting for transverse subgroups
papers.abstract: Transverse subgroups form a special class of discrete subgroups of connected semisimple real algebraic groups that includes all discrete subgroups of rank-one Lie groups, as well as Anosov and relatively Anosov subgroups. We study the joint distribution of partial Cartan projections and the two associated Cartan flags for Zariski dense $\theta$-transverse subgroups. Assuming local mixing of the associated Bowen-Margulis-Sullivan measure, we prove two local limit theorems and deduce counting asymptotics in Euclidean balls and tubes, together with equidistribution of the Cartan flags. These qualitative conclusions hold for $\theta$-Anosov subgroups, for which the local mixing hypothesis is satisfied. If the group is linearly $\theta$-regular near the direction of maximal growth, a polynomial error in local mixing gives polynomial errors in these results. Applying the quantitative local mixing theorem of Kim-Oh-Pan, we obtain local limit and counting theorems with polynomial error estimates for several classes of relatively Anosov representations of Fuchsian groups.

papers.title: Haar local mixing for transverse subgroups
papers.abstract: Transverse subgroups form a special class of discrete subgroups of connected semisimple real algebraic groups that includes all discrete subgroups of rank-one Lie groups, as well as Anosov and relatively Anosov subgroups. For torsion-free Zariski dense $\theta$-transverse subgroups, we establish Haar local mixing for the partial Weyl chamber action under a Bowen-Margulis-Sullivan (BMS) local mixing hypothesis. The proof is based on a transfer principle using the domains of discontinuity introduced by Delarue-Monclair-Sanders and extended to transverse subgroups by Guedes Bonthonneau-Lefeuvre-Weich. For $\theta$-Anosov subgroups, we verify the BMS hypothesis by adapting existing arguments and hence obtain Haar local mixing. As a consequence, we obtain asymptotics for the volume and distribution of long returns and recover the growth indicator from return volumes. Under linear $\theta$-regularity, the transfer also holds with polynomial error estimates. This condition is satisfied by subgroups of $\theta$-Anosov or relatively $\theta$-Anosov groups.

papers.title: Positivity of simplicial volume of convex projective manifolds
papers.abstract: Let $\Omega$ be an irreducible properly convex projective domain admitting a discrete cocompact group action of projective automorphisms. We prove that the Holmes--Thompson volumes of projective simplices with vertices in $\Omega$ are uniformly bounded. As a consequence, we prove that a closed properly convex projective manifold of dimension at least two has positive simplicial volume if and only if it is irreducible.

papers.title: A notion of pseudo-morphisms with applications to the study of polynomial maps and of link-homotopy groups of 2-string link
papers.abstract: We introduce a notion of pseudo-morphism for groups, which extends the notion of group morphism from a group to a ring. We show that pseudo-morphisms from a group $G$ to an integral domain $R$ form a filtred Hopf algebra which can be seen as an efficient notion of dual for $G$. We also show that pseudo-morphisms are closely related to the notion of polynomial maps in the sense of Eilenberg-MacLane/Passi, the two notions even coinciding when $G$ is finitely generated and $R$ is a field. It follows that, in that case, polynomial maps are endowed with an Hopf structure. In a second part, we study non repeated Milnor invariants (in the $4$-dimensional context of $2$-string links) from this pseudo-morphism point of view. We show that they form a sub-bialgebra of the Hopf algebra of pseudo-morphisms on the group of $2$-string links up to link-homotopy, and prove that it is isomorphic to an explicit quotient $\textrm{Mil}$ of a polynomial ring. This leads to a fully algebraic description of the group of 2-string links up to link-homotopy as the dual group associated to $\textrm{Mil}$. As a by-product, we obtain that non repeated Milnor invariants are polynomial maps, and we show that this can be used to give a new proof of their finite type property.

papers.title: Finite generation of the second homology group of the genus three Torelli group
papers.abstract: We prove that the group $H_2(\mathcal{I}_3;\mathbb{Z})$ is finitely generated, where $\mathcal{I}_3$ is the Torelli subgroup of the mapping class group of a closed genus-three surface $\Sigma_3$. A key role in the proof is played by establishing the following property: for each symplectic transvection $t_x\in\mathrm{Sp}_{6}(\mathbb{Z})$, we have $$ \bigl(t^{120}_x-1\bigr)^{57}\bigl(t_x^{24}-1\bigr)(t_x-1)^6H_2(\mathcal{I}_3;\mathbb{Z})=0. $$ The proof is based on the study of the spectral sequences associated with the action of $\mathcal{I}_3$ on the Bestvina-Bux-Margalit complex of minimizing cycles and with the actions on certain auxiliary complexes of the stabilizers of two- and three-component multicurves on $\Sigma_3$. The remaining ingredients are Tavgen's theorem, which asserts that $\mathrm{Sp}_{6}(\mathbb{Z})$ has bounded elementary generation, and the result of Kassabov and Putman, which asserts that $H_2(\mathcal{I}_3;\mathbb{Z})$ is finitely generated as a $\mathbb{Z}[\mathrm{Sp}_6(\mathbb{Z})]$-module.

papers.title: Regular genus of $\mathbb{S}^2 \times \mathbb{S}^1 \times \mathbb{S}^1$, $4$-torus, and small covers over $\Delta^2 \times \Delta^2$
papers.abstract: A crystallization is an edge-colored graph encoding a contracted triangulation of a closed PL manifold, providing a combinatorial framework for studying PL-manifold invariants. In this framework, we determine the regular genus of several important $4$-manifolds. We first prove that $\mathcal{G}(\mathbb{S}^2\times\mathbb{S}^1\times\mathbb{S}^1)=6$, thereby resolving a conjecture on the regular genus of $\mathbb{S}^2\times\mathbb{S}^1\times\mathbb{S}^1$. We also establish that $\mathcal{G}(\mathbb{S}^1\times\mathbb{S}^1\times\mathbb{S}^1\times\mathbb{S}^1)=16$. These computations lead to further observations on the regular genus of the $n$-torus and motivate the conjecture $\mathcal{G}(\mathbb{T}^n)=1+\frac{(n+1)!(n-3)}{8}$ for $n\geq 5$. We then apply our combinatorial methods to small covers. For the simple polytope $\Delta^2\times\Delta^2$, we classify the corresponding small covers up to Davis-Januszkiewicz equivalence and obtain exactly seven equivalence classes. One of these is $\mathbb{RP}^2\times\mathbb{RP}^2$, while the remaining six are $\mathbb{RP}^2$-bundles over $\mathbb{RP}^2$. We prove that all seven small covers have regular genus $8$. Thus, the paper provides regular genus computations for a collection of $4$-manifolds arising from products and small covers. The approach is purely combinatorial and relies on various combinatorial moves.

papers.title: Rank-One Sutured Instanton Homology Detects Homology Products
papers.abstract: We prove that a balanced sutured manifold $(M,\gamma)$ satisfying $\dim_{\mathbb C} SHI(M,\gamma)=1$ is an integral homology product; that is, $H_*(M,R_-(\gamma);\mathbb Z)=H_*(M,R_+(\gamma);\mathbb Z)=0$. Consequently, for every taut balanced sutured manifold $(M,\gamma)$, $SHI(M,\gamma)\cong\mathbb C$ if and only if $(M,\gamma)$ is a product sutured manifold. The proof uses the enhanced Euler characteristic of $SHI$ and a specialization formula for sutured torsion.

papers.title: Determinants of amphichiral knots of braid index at most three
papers.abstract: We show that an odd number n is the determinant of an amphichiral knot of braid index at most three if and only if both n and n + 4 are sums of two squares. The proof rests on the known description of amphichiral knots of braid index three as closures of alternating 3-braid words with a rotation or reflection symmetry (Birman--Menasco, Stoimenov, Jung). Determinant formulas for closed 3-braids are also known (e.g. through the reduced Burau representation at t = -1); what is added here is their evaluation on the two symmetric families, which gives the condition on n + 4, and an explicit construction for the converse. For amphichiral knots of braid index three this describes which determinants occur, which bears on the determinant part of a question of Jung. We did not find the statement in the literature we searched. As a consequence, for an odd n with n + 4 not a sum of two squares, every amphichiral knot with determinant n has braid index at least five; we test this on 4,999 amphichiral knots of Burton's census with up to 19 crossings whose determinant satisfies this hypothesis.

papers.title: Psyquandle Fares
papers.abstract: We introduce a new infinite family of invariants of singular knot and links and of pseudoknots by extending the biquandle fares construction to the case of psyquandles. We give the axioms explicitly for four cases of fare-based invariants: 1-fares, signed crooked 2-fares, signed through 2-fares and signed complete 2-fares. We provide examples of each type, illustrating the method of computation and collecting some results for toy examples using small-cardinality psyquandles and abelian coefficient groups.

papers.title: Legendrian surgery on the unit cotangent bundle of the Klein bottle and infinitely many Stein fillings
papers.abstract: We show that a single Legendrian surgery on the canonical contact structure of the unit cotangent bundle $ST^*K$ of the Klein bottle $K$ produces a planar contact $3$--manifold $(Y,\xi)$ with infinitely many pairwise non-homeomorphic Stein fillings. The fillings are obtained from the disk cotangent bundle $DT^*K$ by attaching a single Weinstein $2$--handle along the images of one Legendrian knot under the powers of a contactomorphism of $(ST^*K,\xi_{\mathrm{can}})$, no positive power of which extends over $DT^*K$. The construction takes place in a planar open book of $(ST^*K,\xi_{\mathrm{can}})$, and $(Y,\xi)$ is contactomorphic to Baykur's recent example of a planar contact $3$--manifold with infinitely many Stein fillings. Since $(ST^*K,\xi_{\mathrm{can}})$ has a unique minimal symplectic filling up to homeomorphism, finiteness of fillings is not preserved under Legendrian surgery, even for planar contact $3$--manifolds. The same construction gives the planar contact $3$--manifolds with infinitely many rational homology ball Stein fillings found earlier by the author.

papers.title: Link Spectra of Lorenz-like Templates and the Horseshoe
papers.abstract: We give a complete classification of the inclusion relations between the link spectrum of the horseshoe template $L(0,1)$ and those of the nonnegative Lorenz-like templates $L(0,a)$. For a template $T$, its link spectrum $\mathscr L(T)$ consists of the link types carried by $T$, allowing parallel strands along its strips. For integers $a\geq0$, the spectra of $L(0,a)$ and $L(0,1)$ are comparable under inclusion if and only if $a\notin\{0,2\}$. More precisely, \[ \mathscr L(L(0,a))=\mathscr L(L(0,1)) \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad a=1, \] while \[ L(0,a)\prec L(0,1) \qquad (a\geq3). \] For $a=0$ and $a=2$, the two spectra are incomparable. The main new containment is \[ L(0,2n)\preceq L(0,1)\qquad(n\geq2), \] which goes beyond the classical parity-preserving nesting relations. A key ingredient is a braid-theoretic criterion: every $T$-link \[ T((r_1,s_1),\ldots,(r_k,s_k)) \] with $s_k\geq2r_k$ is a horseshoe link. This gives a large explicit family belonging to both the Lorenz and horseshoe spectra. In the reverse direction, we construct a horseshoe link outside the Lorenz spectrum. For each integer $m\geq6$, we obtain infinitely many horseshoe links of braid index $m$ excluded from every other nonnegative $L(0,a)$. These examples give infinitely many links with any prescribed number of components at least three. In the other direction, for each positive number of components, we give infinitely many links carried by both $L(0,0)$ and $L(0,2)$ and excluded from the horseshoe spectrum.

papers.title: Braid monodromy and the Cartwright--Steger surface
papers.abstract: Building on the Livne-like construction of Cartwright, Koziarz and Yeung, we construct a closed smooth 4-manifold with a map to the two-sphere whose generic fiber has genus 109 and whose four exceptional fibers are determined by explicit braid and permutation data. A pencil of four-pointed spheres realizes the same global braid monodromy and makes the covering holomorphic. We show that the contraction of its thirty-six exceptional curves is the Cartwright-Steger surface, hence our smooth construction gives a topological description of this complex surface.

papers.title: Goldman's Ergodicity Conjecture and Branched Developing Maps
papers.abstract: We prove that every representation $\rho:\pi_1(\Sigma_g)\rightarrow\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathrm{R})$ which sends every simple closed curve to a hyperbolic element admits a branched developing map. As a corollary, the mapping class group action on the Euler class zero component of the $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathrm{R})$-character variety of a genus $g$ surface is ergodic if $g\geq3$. (The action is not ergodic if $g=2$.) Moreover, almost every representation of nonzero Euler class admits a branched developing map.

papers.title: Hyperbolic string vertices as geometric chains
papers.abstract: For 0<L<=2arcsinh(1), the hyperbolic string vertices of Costello and Zwiebach consist of the bordered hyperbolic surfaces with geodesic boundary of length L whose interior simple closed geodesics have length at least L. We show that the corresponding regions in moduli space are compact oriented orbifolds with corners whose boundaries are, including orientations and automorphism groups, the spaces of twisted sewings. Hence their generating chain satisfies the master equation without the bracket term exactly in a complex of geometric chains. The usual connected form cannot hold exactly for geometric chains; we determine its exact form, show that it holds modulo gluing and covering relations in a complex computing the homology of the moduli spaces, and that the vertex currents are the unique top-dimensional solution. Finally we compare with Costello's homotopical framework. In a strict model given by hyperbolic surfaces with marked boundary points, every solution of his master equation with his initial condition integrates exactly to the vertex currents, up to the sign (-1)^(3g-3+n); such solutions exist, are unique up to homotopy, and correspond to the hyperbolic vertices. Under a continuity assumption on the comparison map and granting the inputs of Costello's homology computation, the hyperbolic vertices represent his homotopy class of solutions, for a completed notion of homotopy.

papers.title: Orbifold Morse Handles I. Morse Indices and Isomorphism Classes of Ordered Handles
papers.abstract: We classify the Morse indices and ordered handles arising from nondegenerate critical points of smooth functions on effective orientable four-dimensional orbifolds. Let $\rho\colon G\to\mathrm{SO}(4)$ be a faithful representation of a finite group. Let $V\subset\mathbb R^4$ be the negative eigenspace of a nondegenerate Hessian that is invariant under $\rho(G)$. The splitting $\mathbb R^4=V\oplus V^\perp$ determines an ordered quotient handle. Two such ordered handles admit an orientation-preserving isomorphism if and only if their negative eigenspaces lie in the same orbit under $N_{\mathrm{SO}(4)}(\rho(G))$. We determine the possible Morse indices and the normalizer orbits for every family in the completed Du Val list.

papers.title: Two categorifications of the Kekul\'e relations
papers.abstract: We give new relations in the kernel of the foam evaluation. As a consequence we obtain categorifications of all the Kelul\'e relations introduced by Morrison. Along the way, we discover an equivalent set of relations for which we provide categorifications as well.

papers.title: Minimal submanifolds and stability in Einstein manifolds
papers.abstract: In this paper, we compute the index and nullity for minimal submanifolds of some complex Einstein spaces. We investigate the stability of these minimal submanifolds and suggest a criterion for instability for some cases. We also compute some higher eigenvalues for the Laplacian of the Berger spheres and provide with an algorithm.

papers.title: Computer-assisted proofs for the fourth algebraic transfer in certain generic degrees
papers.abstract: This paper restructures the author's earlier article in Journal of Homotopy and Related Structures to correct its erroneous invariant-dimension calculations for the fourth Singer algebraic transfer and is written as a replacement for that article. More precisely, we determine the domain and image of the transfer in the degree families $2^{s+t+1}+2^{s+1}-3$ with $t\ne3$ and $2^{s+t}+2^s-2$ with $t\notin\{2,3,4\}$, where $s,t$ are positive integers. Divided-power spikes are basis elements dual to polynomial monomials whose exponents have the form $2^j-1$ for nonnegative integers $j$. Their translates under ${\rm GL}_4(\mathbb F_2)$, the group of invertible $4\times4$ matrices over the field with two elements, generate submodules of the Steenrod kernel, the subspace annihilated by all positive Steenrod squares. We present these submodules as quotients of sums of permutation modules on complete flags, which are chains in $\mathbb F_2^4$ containing one subspace of each dimension $0,1,2,3,4$. Identifying the relation spaces in these presentations gives explicit equivariant comparison isomorphisms. A recursion obtained by separating even and odd exponents in each variable reduces the comparisons to specified identities of finite-dimensional subspaces. These comparisons apply to both complete degree families, including the parameter values omitted from the transfer theorem. Duplication and partial flag embeddings also give theoretical comparisons in specified parameter ranges. As a consequence, Singer's injectivity conjecture holds in rank four in both degree families under the stated parameter restrictions. The cokernel is one-dimensional in homological degree $256$ and zero in every other degree in those ranges.

papers.title: On the connectedness of a minimizing cluster's boundary
papers.abstract: We verify that an isoperimetric minimizing cluster on a simply connected homogeneous Riemannian manifold with at most one end always has connected boundary. In particular, the boundary of a single-bubble isoperimetric minimizer on such manifolds must be connected, and hence all isoperimetric sets and their complements must be connected. This is demonstrably false without the simple connectedness assumption or the restriction on the number of ends.

papers.title: Completeness of closed Kleinian flat Pseudo-Riemannian Manifolds of Signature (2,2)
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb{R}^{2,2}$ denote the model space of flat pseudo-Riemannian manifolds of signature $(2,2)$. We prove that the only domain divisible by a discrete subgroup of the isometry group of $\mathbb{R}^{2,2}$ is $\mathbb{R}^{2,2}$ itself. In the Kleinian setting, this provides the first completeness theorem of closed flat pseudo-Riemannian manifolds beyond the Euclidean and Lorentzian cases. Along the proof, we show as a result of independent interest concerning the existence of syndetic hulls in semidirect products $R \ltimes G$, where $G$ is a homothety Lie group. This construction generalizes earlier constructions in affine geometry due to Carri\`ere and Dal'bo.

papers.title: Satellite knots that cannot be represented by positive braids with full twists
papers.abstract: A positive braid with at least one full twist is known to be a minimal braid, i.e, it achieves the braid index for its closure. In this paper we find knots that are the closure of positive minimal braids that cannot be represented by positive braids with full twists. More precisely, we show that some satellite knots with companions and patterns given as the closure of positive braids cannot be represented as the closure of positive braids with full twists. As a consequence, we find infinitely many satellite knots with companions and patterns being Lorenz knots that are not Lorenz knots. This gives an answer to the question whether a satellite knot having Lorenz pattern and companion is also a Lorenz knot, originally addressed by Birman and Williams in a special case in the 1980s.

papers.title: The linear minimal 4-chart with three crossings
papers.abstract: Charts are oriented labeled graphs in a disk. Every simple surface braid ($2$-dimensional braid) can be described by a chart. Moreover, a chart represents an oriented closed surface embedded in four-space. In this paper, we study such embedded surfaces using charts. Let $\Gamma$ be a chart. Let ${\rm Cross}(\Gamma)$ denote the set of all the crossings of $\Gamma$, and let $\Gamma_m$ denote the union of all the edges of label $m$. A 4-chart $\Gamma$ is said to be ${\it linear}$ if every connected component of $$(\Gamma_1\cup \Gamma_3)-{\rm Cross}(\Gamma)$$ is acyclic. In this paper, we prove that after deleting free edges and hoops, every linear minimal $4$-chart with three crossings is lor-equivalent (equivalent under label changes, orientation reversals, and reflections) to the chart describing a $2$-twist-spun trefoil knot.
